title: Chapter 88: The Truth
html:
The woman’s cooperation eased Chen Ge’s suspicion. He stepped forward and picked up the drawing. It showed a black building crowded with red figures. One conspicuous black figure stood apart, as though the red ones were afraid to approach it.

“You say I’m in the drawing. What’s your evidence?” One picture was not enough to convince Chen Ge.

“The people in Fan Yu’s drawings have always been red. This is the first time I’ve seen a black figure. I thought about it for a long time and concluded it must be you, because you’re the only outsider to visit our home in the past month.” Fan Yu’s aunt stood in the corner, water dripping from her raincoat in an unnerving rhythm.

“That’s all? Then what do the red figures mean? What’s the difference between red and black?”

Fan Yu’s aunt studied Chen Ge in silence. Just as he decided she would not answer, she said, “The red figures are ghosts. Since I’ve only seen one black figure, I assume it represents a living person.”

“Ghosts?”

“I know you won’t believe me, but some things in this world defy explanation,” Fan Yu’s aunt said with the calm of someone who had rehearsed the speech many times. “Even before the accident, I knew Fan Yu could see things other people couldn’t. I told his parents, but they didn’t believe in ghosts.”

“Since they didn’t believe it, why do you?” Chen Ge’s curiosity was piqued.

“At first, no one knew Fan Yu had this ability. Then my husband and two children died in a car accident. It was the darkest time of my life. Whenever I broke down over their photographs, Fan Yu would bring me his drawings—two small red children living in a black house. He said they were his brother and sister.”

Warmth softened the woman’s eyes. “Of course I didn’t believe him at first. I thought he was only trying to comfort me. But as he drew more pictures, my certainty wavered. I asked what his brother and sister were doing, and his answers were astonishingly precise. Sometimes he mentioned little habits only their mother could have known.”

“That’s when you believed Fan Yu could see ghosts?”

“Yes. Or perhaps I only wanted it to be true. Sometimes I even see my own children in Fan Yu.”

“Even if what you’re saying is true, a child’s painting still represents nothing. Don’t tell me every human that appears in his drawing will die?” Chen Ge asked cautiously.

“Turn the paper over.”

Chen Ge did as instructed. Another drawing covered the reverse: an old well from which several unusually vivid red figures were climbing, with a black figure standing beside it. Curiously, the black figure occupied exactly the same position as the one before the black house on the other side.

“Legend says an old well at this school has claimed many lives. The ghosts are climbing out, and you’re standing beside it. They’ve targeted you. If you stay any longer, something may happen.” Fan Yu’s aunt sounded sincere, almost genuinely concerned for him.

Chen Ge studied both sides. As he compared them, a slight frown touched his face and an answer settled in his mind.

“Looks like I misunderstood you.” Chen Ge slipped Fan Yu’s drawing into his pocket, silently announcing that he would not return it. “I was planning to leave anyway. Let’s go together and watch each other’s backs. This place gives me the creeps.”

“You’re right.” Fan Yu’s aunt nodded and approached. Appearing to trust her completely, Chen Ge turned away and exposed his defenseless back.

They set off single file. Chen Ge moved slowly, mallet in hand. Behind him, Fan Yu’s aunt seemed afraid of being left alone and gradually quickened her pace. Had anyone seen Chen Ge’s face, the cold calculation in his eyes would have shocked them.

As the gap between them closed, Fan Yu’s aunt’s expression changed. Her face tightened, and the hand concealed beneath her raincoat lunged toward Chen Ge, clutching something sharp.

“I knew there was something wrong with you.” Chen Ge reacted faster than she expected and with greater ruthlessness. The mallet struck her hand; a kick followed.

BANG!

Fan Yu’s aunt slammed into the tiled wall, and the object in her hand clattered to the floor. Chen Ge approached and found a small paring knife, the kind used to debone meat, its edge viciously sharp.

Hair hanging across her face, Fan Yu’s aunt rose like a vengeful ghost. Chen Ge gave her no chance to retaliate and ‘helped’ her back to the floor.

“I’ve suspected you since I visited your place, but I could not find any proof. Now, you’ve finally shown me your true face.”

The difference in strength was obvious. Fan Yu’s aunt tried several times to rise and failed. She could only glare at him with naked hatred. “How did you know?”

“I never trusted you. This drawing gave me the proof I needed—the picture on the back is yours. Did you really think a child’s style would be so easy to imitate? Don’t glare at me. You made the mistake. If you don’t want to be exposed, don’t commit the crime.” Chen Ge picked up the paring knife, its blade gleaming coldly in the dark. “You killed Fan Yu’s parents, didn’t you? Whatever your reason, how could you murder your own family in cold blood?”

“It was never my intention to kill! You have no idea what really happened that night!” Fan Yu’s aunt lashed out at Chen Ge.

“Maybe not, but one thing is certain—you were involved.” Chen Ge considered how to restrain her until the police arrived.

“The real killer is Fan Yu’s father!”

“You’re blaming a dead man? That’s your defense?” After making sure she carried no other weapons, Chen Ge relaxed slightly.

“It’s true.” Fan Yu’s aunt slumped to the floor, and the truth buried for years finally spilled out. “By now, you must know what kind of sick bastard my brother was. In this very toilet, he drove an innocent girl mad. I later heard she was forced to take her own life. Afterward, my brother grew even more unstable and paranoid, always insisting someone was coming for him. My sister-in-law could endure no more and filed for divorce, but he refused to let her go. Driven into a corner, she threatened to expose his crimes unless he agreed.”
